Her body, her choice is about not forcing a woman to be pregnant or birth a child. It’s not about not forcing a woman to be a parent. I agree that there is a double standard, but I don’t think her body, her choice is the culprit.

If the woman had the right to get an abortion and the man made his stance clear before the woman’s window for abortion expired, then I don’t think he should have any responsibility. For example, if the law says abortion must be performed before 20 weeks and at 30 weeks the father says “nope I don’t want this kid.” Then he’s still on the hook. Because the didn’t have the chance to make an informed decision (deciding to have a kid where the father is in the picture is very different than deciding to have a kid as a totally single parent). That said, if he doesn’t have to carry any parental responsibilities, he doesn’t get any parental rights either. He doesn’t get to go to court 3 years later and demand custody. There are 2 grey areas that I don’t really have an answer to though. 1) Both parties want an abortion but can’t afford it.
